races.name: Spillers Future Champions Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: Arrives in excellent recent form (two wins from last four, both over this trip on good ground), leads by default in this field and his trainer Hannon sends him in with strong stable form; the STYLE_FIT flag is academic here as he is genuinely expected to front-run rather than race out of role.|

runners_data.name: Farasi Lane
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on good ground 11 days ago and arrives in cracking nick for Micky Hammond, but gets on tongue tie and naturally wants to race prominently — this field means he is unlikely to get as close to the pace as he'd prefer, which is a material tactical disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Happy Banner
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's consistent mare has placed in seven of fourteen starts on good ground without winning, wears hood and tongue tie, and though she's genuine around a mile on turf, her natural desire to race up with the pace will be frustrated by Best Rate already occupying that position.|

runners_data.name: Jungle Ruler
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with limited placed form on good ground (1 placing from 8 runs) ridden by 7lb claimer Toby Moore; his consistent mid-pack finishes suggest he sits in a race well but lacks the decisive acceleration to win unless the front-runner comes back to him.|

runners_data.name: Brocklesby Bill
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up horse in the race, wearing hood, with a genuine win over 7f on good ground recently and course form — but in a slowly-run five-runner race with one pace-setter, the late ground he needs to make up may simply never materialise.|

races.paceDynamic: Best Rate is the only confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and should lead uncontested from the gate, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over the mile at Sandown. With no genuine rival willing to press for the lead, Best Rate will dictate fractions at his own tempo, which historically favours the horse in front on a flat, galloping track like Sandown. Farasi Lane and Happy Banner are natural prominent racers who would ordinarily dispute for the early positions, but with Best Rate already filling that role and the field compressed, both are mapped to midfield — the field holds more prominent types than can comfortably hold that position, and Best Rate is the horse most likely to actually lead with Jungle Ruler perhaps tracking loosely. The race shape strongly favours a pace-pressing or prominent profile that can sit just off Best Rate's controlled fractions and deliver a sustained challenge from two furlongs out — true hold-up tactics look disadvantaged in a slowly-run five-runner affair.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Best Rate Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Best Rate is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop throughout and no rival applies early pressure.
scenarios.body: Best Rate sets fractions entirely to suit himself, covering the mile at Sandown without ever being headed or hurried, leaving a stamina-based closer like Brocklesby Bill with too little to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Farasi Lane or Happy Banner push forward early and manage to secure closer contact than their mapped position suggests, pressuring Best Rate from the turn.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace quickens the race enough to expose Best Rate late, with the two prominent types who secured early positions better placed to capitalise in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Brocklesby Bill Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — driven by a contested early gallop — to soften the leaders and allow a hold-up finisher to close ground through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill, a true hold-up horse with a recent course win over the trip in similar going, times a run from the rear as the leaders tie up, but this scenario relies on a pace that this small field may simply not generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jungle Ruler Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Jungle Ruler settles in a perfect position just behind Best Rate, bides time racing prominently, and produces a clean turn of foot rounding the home bend.
scenarios.body: Jungle Ruler's consistent placed form at this trip and on good ground gives him a platform if the pace is just right, but his OR of 84 and apprentice jockey (7lb claimer Toby Moore) make the execution uncertain against a leader in control.

watchPoints.text: Best Rate has won twice over this exact trip on good ground in the last 12 days — if he jumps cleanly and leads unchallenged, his rivals are under immediate pressure to close a gap they may never properly bridge.

Farasi Lane and Happy Banner both want to race prominently — watch the first furlong to see whether either pushes forward more aggressively than expected, because if they do, it transforms the race into a more contested affair that changes every scenario probability.

Brocklesby Bill's hold-up style is entirely dependent on pace being strong enough to soften the leaders — in a five-runner flat mile with a single front-runner, monitor whether she finds herself stranded when the leaders don't come back.

Jungle Ruler's 7lb apprentice Toby Moore has limited race-reading experience at Sandown; watch whether Moore tracks Best Rate closely enough from the off or allows too big a gap to develop before the home turn.

races.name: Spillers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Justcallmepete
runners_data.note: Confirmed lead horse and the sole genuine pace-setter in this field; drops back to 5f from a recent 6f campaign and seven-day fitness is fine at 48 days, but style-fit tag suggests discounting if not dictating — the key question is whether the prominent press from Novelette and Hypnotised unsettles its rhythm.

runners_data.name: Wheels Of Fire
runners_data.note: Sole true hold-up runner in the field, giving this one a unique profile; won over course and distance at 5f on soft in latest outing and goes well fresh at 58 days, but must rely on the pace hotting up sufficiently to reel in the prominent racers.

runners_data.name: Atticum
runners_data.note: Unclassified style makes reading this runner difficult; three-year-old from Robert Cowell's yard who has form on good over 5f and 6f, though limited winning form in similar conditions (3/6 sim-going) and Cowell runs only occasionally at present with 0 from 10 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Novelette
runners_data.note: Strong candidate for this race shape — Simon and Ed Crisford three-year-old with two wins over 5f on good, prominent racing style fits perfectly behind the lone front runner; Callum Rodriguez rides and the yard has had four winners from 19 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Hypnotised
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton three-year-old whose sole win came on a standard surface but whose prominent style suits the projected race shape; 96 days since last run is the standout flag here, and going form on good (2 from 4 attempts) is workable if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Rage Of Thunder
runners_data.note: In-form runner on a 20-day turnaround with two wins from nine on good ground; Gary Moore's yard is ticking over (1/12 in 14 days) but this is a true prominent type forced into a midfield berth by the traffic ahead, and the style-fit discount is real — its best form comes when driving forward unchallenged.

runners_data.name: Army Bugler
runners_data.note: Long absence (306 days) is a major concern that eclipses all other angles; Warren Greatrex sends this three-year-old back after over ten months off, and though the form on good ground is solid (1 win, 2 places from 5), the ring-rustiness combined with being mapped out of its natural prominent role makes this a significant risk.

races.paceDynamic: Justcallmepete is the confirmed front runner here and, with only one true pace-setter in a seven-runner field over five furlongs at Sandown, the tempo is likely to be honest rather than frenetic — a controlled, uncontested lead that suits those who can track close to the pace. Novelette and Hypnotised are both genuine prominent types who should press from close up, meaning the race will be run in a tight, compact group with the lead covered from the front three stalls. This field holds more prominent-minded horses than the shape can accommodate: Rage Of Thunder and Army Bugler are both natural front-runners who have been redistributed to a midfield mapping because Justcallmepete and the prominent types will dominate the early berths; both are likely to find themselves racing wider or later than they would prefer. The race shape overwhelmingly favours a horse who can sit second or third, travel within a length or two of the pace, and produce a decisive turn of foot from two furlongs out — a prominent-to-challenge profile is the clear beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Leaders Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Justcallmepete controls a measured gallop and the prominent trackers Novelette and Hypnotised travel fluently in behind, the front trio dictate throughout.
scenarios.body: Justcallmepete sets a sustainable clip with Novelette and Hypnotised covering the move, and with no genuine closer to reel them in, the race is decided between those who raced prominently from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to soften the lead and a prominent chaser produces a sharper late kick from second or third.
scenarios.body: Novelette or Hypnotised sits a length off Justcallmepete, quickens past at the two-pole and holds on as the leader weakens slightly in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front runners tie each other up, creating a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Wheels Of Fire, the only true hold-up type in the field, gets a clear run up the stands rail and picks up ground in the final furlong as leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistribution Resolved
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent glut causes early scrimmaging and Rage Of Thunder or Army Bugler force their way into their natural front positions, disrupting the settled pace picture.
scenarios.body: A messy, rough race opens the door for a horse who finds daylight mid-pack, but given both Rage Of Thunder and Army Bugler carry out-of-role penalties their chance of winning this shape remains modest even if they get position.

watchPoints.text: Novelette and Hypnotised are both genuine prominent types — watch whether they attempt to press Justcallmepete early, because if both crowd the leader in the first two furlongs the race could become a battle for position before the turn.

Army Bugler is returning from 306 days off; watch the market moves closely in the pre-race period, as any significant support would suggest stable confidence despite the layoff and would elevate its in-race danger markedly.

Rage Of Thunder is mapped to midfield but is a natural front-runner — watch the early strides to see whether Jason Watson pushes forward to claim a prominent position, which would change the pace dynamic entirely and may lead to a faster-than-anticipated gallop.

Wheels Of Fire is the only horse with a genuine hold-up profile; watch whether Joe Leavy gets a clean passage up the inside or rail, as in a tight seven-runner field over Sandown's five furlongs, traffic can be an issue for any genuine closer who needs a run to materialise.

races.name: Chasemore Farm Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Spillers Winners Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Rod Millman three-year-old who operates as a genuine hold-up horse, returning after 16 days; recent form is modest and his Good-going record (two runs, zero wins, zero places) offers little encouragement, though light weight of 135lbs keeps him competitive on paper.

runners_data.name: Santiago Boy
runners_data.note: Charles Hills handler has had a quiet recent record (2/15 in 14 days) and this hold-up type has raced exclusively at 7f or 8f on Standard or Good ground with just one placed effort from four similar runs; the hood may sharpen his focus but he hasn't shown enough to suggest a win is imminent.

runners_data.name: Sydney Rock
runners_data.note: Consistent placer — five seconds in his last five — who goes well as a hold-up horse but has never converted; returns after 16 days and his one comparable Good-ground run produced a place, though his lack of a winning strike is a concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Home Hero
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner has dropped in trip from 10f and is equipped with a visor; a natural hold-up horse pushed toward midfield on the map because hold-up slots are oversubscribed, and the step down in distance combined with four runs without a win raises doubts about whether he can deliver here even if he gets a good run.

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's gelding has a win on Good ground at 9f (form: 1/9f/GOO) and is the most form-credible of the hold-up contingent; placed on Good going from four attempts, though his natural style means he needs Ingemar to set a searching enough pace to make his finishing kick count.

runners_data.name: Galba
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with three placed efforts from five runs on Good, returning after 47 days which is a flag worth monitoring; pushed onto the map in midfield because the hold-up cluster is too large — his best chance is if he can settle in a forward enough position to make a meaningful move.

runners_data.name: Terranoble
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's charge won at 8f on Standard (1/8f/STA) and comes here after a lengthy 67-day absence, which is a significant fitness concern; a true hold-up type whose position on the map is a function of field congestion rather than natural style, and his layoff makes it hard to trust him at this stage.

runners_data.name: Ingemar
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field and the pivotal tactical factor in the race; Brian Meehan's gelding wears a hood and has finished 5-7-9 in three runs, so his form is limited, but uncontested control of the pace from the front gives him a disproportionate chance to dictate and potentially steal a march on the hold-up field.

runners_data.name: Bennyworth
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's lowest-rated runner (OR 55) is a hold-up horse returning after just 13 days; has six recent runs without a win and a modest placed record, and with the field already overloaded with closers, the task of threading through traffic from the rear looks beyond him at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Ingemar is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and should bowl along uncontested on the front end, setting a genuine but manageable tempo over the mile trip at Sandown. With no other natural pace horse to challenge or pressure him, Ingemar can dictate his own rhythm and control the race from the front, which on Good ground over a flat mile is a significant tactical advantage. The entire remainder of the field is made up of hold-up horses, meaning the closers will face a steady, organised gallop and must produce their finishing kicks from off the pace without the benefit of a strong pace to chase. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or at least in the first half of the field and challenge Ingemar from a position of tactical control — deep closers face a difficult task if the gallop is unhurried. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can genuinely fill rear positions; Galba, Sogniamo, Home Hero, Terranoble, and Bennyworth are all natural hold-up horses mapped forward because there is simply no other pace in the race, meaning several will race out of their preferred role and may not produce their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ingemar controls, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Ingemar bowls along at a sustainable pace and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ingemar sets an uncontested rhythm, gets the race on his own terms, and the closers — forced wide or unable to quicken from deep — simply cannot reel him in before the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to set up a closing run and one of the true hold-up horses gets a dream passage through.
scenarios.body: A horse like Sogniamo or Home Hero, both with proven hold-up form, times a run from midfield to cut down a tiring Ingemar in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield presser pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed horse settles just behind Ingemar, travels strongly, and kicks when asked at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Galba or Terranoble, racing more prominently than their natural style, take advantage of the strong vantage point and collar the leader in the Sandown straight before the deep closers can land a blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ingemar sets a falsely slow tempo and the field concertinas, creating a sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a bunched tactical affair in the straight and a horse with a sharp turn of foot like Sydney Rock or Next Guilian finds a gap to win in a rough-and-tumble finish.

watchPoints.text: Ingemar sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo — if Joe Leavy pings him from the gate and gets a clear lead within the first two furlongs, the hold-up field may never see him again.

Sogniamo and Home Hero are both natural hold-up horses who need a proper gallop; if Ingemar dawdles, both risk being caught in a sprint finish that does not suit their profile despite their form credentials.

Terranoble's 67-day absence for Denis Coakley is the longest lay-off in the field — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages, particularly since he must race out of his natural hold-up role.

Galba's 47-day break and redistribution to midfield on the map mean Jack Mitchell will need to make a quick decision about positioning at the start — if he is unable to slot in behind Ingemar, his chance is compromised.

Sydney Rock has placed in five of his last five starts without winning — if the pace is truly moderate, his consistent finishing form could finally convert, but the pattern of near-misses is a genuine concern.

races.name: Spillers Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kimeko Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with 9/15 sim-going record who stays 1m2f well, though her recent form string of 285450 makes it hard to trust she has the finishing kick to reel in a non-pressured leader from off the pace today.

runners_data.name: Celestias Comet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who wears headgear and has Charles Fanshawe patience behind her; her sole win came over 10f on good and her profile suits tracking a slow pace here, though she has been beaten in her last five.

runners_data.name: Ammoony
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and pace anchor for this race; runs here from her natural lead position but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) reminds that she is rated prominent rather than a true solo leader — her chance rests on dictating terms undisturbed from a 72-day break.

runners_data.name: Take A View
runners_data.note: Unknown style horse with a tidy place record in three career starts at 8-10f on good, wearing tongue tie; inexperience limits the read but she has placed on every going-similar start, and Charlton's 1/6 14-day record is modest.

runners_data.name: Melody De Vega
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 10f on good gives her strong form credentials here; hold-up style means she needs the pace to be honest but she is 15 days fresh and Callum Rodriguez's positive booking adds confidence.

runners_data.name: Lady Milton
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo prominent racer with two wins on easy surfaces and a consistent string of places on good going; Rob Hornby is a smart tactical jockey for this trip and her profile fits the predicted race shape as well as any runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who is shown in midfield only because the field is over-stocked with closers; her 9/12 sim-going record is solid but a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 and a crowded rear section combine to suppress her realistic chance of landing a clean run.

runners_data.name: Pershalla
runners_data.note: Last ran just six days ago and wears headgear; a genuine hold-up horse whose true position has been displaced by the weight of closers in this field — her 0W1P sim-going record on turf-good and low OR of 62 make it hard to construct a bullish case even if she does secure a clean passage.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a P headgear flag stepping up from sprint trips; her sim-going figures are decent (4/6) but she has not won and her form has come over shorter distances, making this 10f trip a step into the unknown for a horse needing cover.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Athene
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose sole turf-good run produced a second over 10f — directly relevant form; Ashley Lewis claims 5lb and Ed Walker's 10/36 14-day record is the busiest and most productive of any trainer here, worth noting.

races.paceDynamic: Ammoony is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press her from the gates, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m2f trip at Sandown. The prominent types Lady Milton, Celestias Comet and Spirit Of Athene will likely slot in directly behind her, creating an orderly procession rather than a contested early pace. With the going unknown but the surface turf and the race shape pointing toward a steady-to-moderate tempo, horses with the tactical speed to travel prominently and pick off a non-pressured leader have the structural advantage — specifically those who can track Ammoony through the final bend and produce a clean, sustained finish up the straight. Come On Eibhlin and Pershalla are genuine hold-up horses whose natural position at the rear is compromised by the volume of similar types in this field, with Lady Milton and Celestias Comet most likely to actually secure their preferred prominent berths; those displaced closers cannot be expected to produce their typical pattern.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ammoony Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ammoony sets a measured, uncontested tempo and the prominent trackers produce a clean turn-of-foot from just off her heels.
scenarios.body: Ammoony controls the race without a rival forcing the pace, and a horse sitting second or third can reel her in up the Sandown straight without expending energy fighting for position early; Lady Milton and Celestias Comet are ideally placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely slow enough that Ammoony's controlled lead turns into an unassailable advantage and no rival delivers enough finish.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling pace flatters the horse on the front end, and Ammoony's recent form — winning twice at 1m and 1m2f on good — shows she can quicken off a slow tempo; prominent horses who track her get caught flat-footed if the gaps have already opened.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens materially in the middle stages and midfield horses get a clear run up the rail or widest route to swamp the leaders.
scenarios.body: Melody De Vega and Kimeko Glory carry genuine hold-up form at 1m2f on good going and, if the pace is strong enough to string the field out, they can pick off tiring prominent horses in the final furlong; this scenario requires an untypically honest gallop for this configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the field is genuinely compressed and a clean passage allows a deep hold-up horse to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This shape depends on Come On Eibhlin or Pershalla finding clear air, but both are redistributed from their natural position and their STYLE_FIT tags mark them as less likely to produce their best from a compromised tactical berth; the probability is low precisely because the race shape does not facilitate their true closing pattern.

watchPoints.text: Ammoony's 72-day break is the single biggest unknown — watch whether she settles cleanly in front or shows signs of fresh-horse behaviour that inflates the pace and destroys her own advantage.

Lady Milton and Celestias Comet are both bidding for the same prominent position behind Ammoony — watch the opening furlong to see which secures the cleaner pitch, as the one pushed wider or back will be racing against her natural shape.
Melody De Vega is 15 days fresh off a win and if Callum Rodriguez elects to take closer order than usual rather than sit last, she becomes a significantly more dangerous proposition in Scenario A.

Come On Eibhlin and Pershalla are both genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to field congestion — if either secures an unexpected prominent pitch, revisit their chances sharply upward, but do not expect it.

The going is listed as unknown across all Sandown tracks — if an update confirms soft or heavy, Ammoony's chance recedes markedly (her only soft run produced a 4th) and hold-up horses with give-ground form would benefit.

races.name: Spillers Spectacular Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's 3yo hold-up performer has a win over 12f on good ground and carries a hood (headgear), suggesting she needs to be switched on — the unanswered question is whether 1m6f stretches her stamina, but her form over a mile and a half on good ground is the strongest piece of evidence in her favour; 26 days since last run is straightforward.

runners_data.name: Outflank
runners_data.note: Trained by John & Thady Gosden, who are 7/15 in the last 14 days, this 3yo has consistent placing form at 10-12f on good and soft, but has been off 40 days and is making a step up in trip to 1m6f that her recent runs do not obviously confirm she stays; the fitting of a hood is notable.

runners_data.name: Kakirra
runners_data.note: Four-time winner in a row with victories at 10f, 12f, 12f and 14f, this Ollie Sangster 3yo is primed for this trip, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is worth noting — Kakirra's natural style is closer to prominent than the classic pace-setter, and Rob Hornby may not be aggressive enough to guarantee the front; that said, in a four-runner field with no other pace, she will likely end up on or near the lead regardless.

runners_data.name: Boilermaker
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's 3yo has excellent consistency, placing in four of five recent runs over 12f on good ground, but is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — only 11 days since his last run (the shortest turnaround in the field) and carrying the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92), his chance hinges on a pace collapse that is unlikely when Kakirra controls the race solo; treat his midfield map position as a positional consequence, not his preferred racing style.

races.paceDynamic: Kakirra is the sole confirmed front-runner in a four-horse field and will dictate terms unchallenged from the off over 1m6f at Sandown, setting a controlled, unhurried tempo on good ground. With no rival likely to contest the lead, this shapes as a truly uncontested lead scenario — Kakirra can bowl along at a comfortable gallop, conserving energy and controlling the pace from wire to wire. The three hold-up horses (Last Verse, Outflank, and Boilermaker, the latter redistributed to midfield on the map despite being a true hold-up type) will be forced to track from behind, meaning the closers must generate their own momentum late. This race shape strongly favours the front-running profile: a lone pace-setter on good ground over a staying trip with no pressure is a textbook setup for the leader to be very hard to peg back, while genuine hold-up horses need a true pace to exploit — and that is absent here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kakirra Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kakirra bowls clear from the start and sets a sustainable solo tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Kakirra has won four consecutive races at distances up to 14f and races prominently, and with no rival to press her she can dictate every yard, quickening or conserving as Rob Hornby sees fit. A lone pace-setter on good ground over 1m6f with back-markers unable to generate sufficient late momentum is a near-ideal scenario for the leader to hold on comfortably.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kakirra sets a slightly too-strong gallop and ties up in the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Last Verse has shown stamina form over 12f on good ground with a win at that trip and carries blinkers suggesting she needs motivation — a strong end to the race would suit her profile best. Outflank has placed at 12f on good ground twice and the step up to 1m6f is the question, but a genuine end-to-end gallop would give her the chance to pick off a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Boilermaker Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and Boilermaker, despite being a true hold-up type mapped to midfield, produces a strong staying finish.
scenarios.body: Boilermaker has placed in four of his last five starts over 12f on good ground and has the consistent form to be dangerous if the race is truly run to suit late closers. However, as a genuine hold-up type redistributed on the map, he is unlikely to be ideally positioned and his chance depends on a pace scenario that may not materialise in this small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outflank Surprises Field
scenarios.trigger: If Outflank, stepping back up to 1m6f, produces a career-best effort at the trip with the John & Thady Gosden yard in form.
scenarios.body: Outflank has recent form showing 7/15 for the stable in the last 14 days and has placed at 12f on good and soft ground, but her form at the full 1m6f trip is untested from her recent history. This is the most speculative shape and requires both a career-best performance and a race that sets up perfectly for hold-up horses — conditions that are unlikely to align here.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Rob Hornby actively takes Kakirra to the front — if she idles into a prominent rather than leading role, the pace may collapse entirely and open the race up for late closers.

Last Verse's hood (headgear) is worth monitoring in the paddock — if she is reluctant to settle or shows signs of freshness after 26 days off, her hold-up style may be compromised in a small, slowly-run field.
Boilermaker's 11-day turnaround is the shortest in the field — watch for any signs of fatigue or below-par performance that might indicate the quick reappearance is taking a toll.

With only four runners and a single genuine pace-setter, watch for a falsely slow early gallop that compresses the field — in that scenario the final two furlongs become a sprint, which may flatter the horse with the highest top speed rather than the most stamina.

Outflank's stable (John & Thady Gosden, 7/15 in 14 days) is in excellent current form — if she handles the step up to 1m6f, her trainer's recent strike rate makes her a live outsider worth noting for place purposes.
